issues.claim: Sources bullet 1: clients working 'directly with our partners' is cited to https://www.wileylavender.com/our-attorneys
issues.problem: Citation precision only, not a factual error: the exact phrase 'working directly with our partners' appears on the home page (core-values section), while /our-attorneys carries only 'personal attention from our partners'. The two-attorney roster and the 'schedule a consultation by calling our office or filling out the contact form' FAQ answer are both on /our-attorneys, so the bullet mixes two pages.
issues.fix: Split the citation: quote 'directly with our partners' to https://www.wileylavender.com/ and keep https://www.wileylavender.com/our-attorneys for the two Partner listings and the booking-by-phone-or-form answer.

issues.claim: Section 1 Impact: 'about 66-245 staff hours a year (400-700 inquiries, 25-35 minutes each, 40-60% removed)'
issues.problem: Arithmetic is correct and the low-end rate is conservative, but the 400-700 inquiry base is an assumption derived from the site's self-reported 200+ cases/year at 2-3 inquiries per case (it is labelled as an inference in analysis.json, not in the audit). A partner reading it cannot see where the base comes from.
issues.fix: Add four words of provenance, e.g. '400-700 inquiries (estimated from your 200+ cases a year)'. Same fix applies to Section 2's '200 matters' and Section 3's '3-5 hours a week'.

issues.claim: Email draft: 'a two-partner firm handling 200+ matters a year'
issues.problem: Minor wording drift: the site says '200+ successful cases per year' (self-reported marketing) and the audit intro correctly attributes it to the site; the email restates it as unattributed fact and swaps 'cases' for 'matters'.
issues.fix: Use 'the 200+ cases a year your site reports' so the claim stays attributed and matches the source wording.

issues.claim: Section 3 Impact annualisation: '62-130 staff hours a year (3-5 hours a week of chasing, 40-50% removed)'
issues.problem: Methodological nit, not an error: 3-5 hours x 52 weeks x 40-50% assumes 52 working weeks, so the figure is roughly 4-6% high versus a 48-49 week year.
issues.fix: Either say '3-5 hours a week' and leave the annual figure as an approximation, or note the 52-week basis in the parenthetical.
